 Order
The applicant has filed this first application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 12.08.2023 in connection with Crime No.19 of 2023 registered at Police Station Padav District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 409, 34 of IPC.

As per prosecution story, an agreement was entered into by Four Chatur Associates for the sale of certain plots, but the plots were neither sold nor the amount was refunded, as a result of which the present case was registered against the present applicant and other co-accused persons.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is contended that the present bail application has been moved on the ground of prejudice caused due to the inordinate delay in conclusion of the trial.
The applicant has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:382 2 MCRC-57369-2025 in custody since 12.08.2023 and the trial is not likely to conclude in the near future.
It is further submitted that the applicant is a permanent resident of District Gwalior and there is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

In view of the aforesaid circumstances, it is prayed that Narayandas Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58448663/
1 the applicant be extended the benefit of bail.

sentences.text: 5. Learned Panel Lawyer for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

6. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.
Bail is a manifestation of the right to personal liberty, which cannot be denied on uncertain or indefinite factors, particularly when the delay in trial is not attributable to the accused.

Considering the prejudice caused by the delayed trial and in view of the right to a speedy trial enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, it prima facie appears that the applicant's right to speedy trial has been breached.

8. Considering the aforesaid and the fact that the material placed on record does not disclose the possibility of the applicant's fleeing from justice, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.
9. Accordingly, without commenting on merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before it on the dates given by the concerned Court.

The applicant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be;
4.
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
11. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
